post-cm04-linear-damping-model.title: "The damped oscillator model: a harmonic restoring force with a phenomenological linear drag $-c\\dot x$, $c\\ge0$"
post-cm04-linear-damping-model.physical_scope: "Adoption of the damped oscillator as a restricted one-dimensional model: the harmonic restoring force with spring constant k>0 combined, through additive composition of force contributions, with a linear drag force -c x-dot of declared drag coefficient c>=0 (kilograms per second). The drag term is phenomenological: it represents the net effect of a medium that is not modelled, is adopted for a stated regime (viscous, velocity-proportional resistance at small speeds), neglects the random component of the environment's force, and is a different model from quadratic drag or Coulomb friction outside that regime. The item asserts no value of c, no derivation of the drag law, no fluctuation theory and no measured result."

post-cm04-sinusoidal-drive-model.title: "The sinusoidally driven oscillator model: a prescribed external force $f_0\\cos(\\Omega t)$ added to the damped oscillator"
post-cm04-sinusoidal-drive-model.physical_scope: "Adoption of the driven oscillator as a restricted one-dimensional model: the damped oscillator with parameters m>0, k>0, c>=0 together with an external driving force f(t)=f_0 cos(Omega t) of declared amplitude f_0 and angular frequency Omega>0, prescribed as a function of time and independent of the motion. The drive is an idealization of an apparatus or background that maintains a fixed sinusoidal force; it is adopted for a stated regime, its amplitude and frequency are model parameters, and no measured value, no back-reaction model, no non-sinusoidal waveform and no claim that a given apparatus realizes the model is asserted."

post-cm05-central-model.title: "Adopted central-force model class: static central pair potentials, the reduced one-label problem, the fixed-centre idealization, reading conventions and exclusions"
post-cm05-central-model.physical_scope: "Adoption of the page's central-force model class inside the framework's force and interaction branches: two-label models presented by a static $C^2$ central pair potential on a collision-excluded annulus and free of external forces; the reduced one-label problem of mass $\\mu$; the separate one-label fixed-centre idealization; the reading conventions for force centre, orbit and body labels; and the explicit exclusions (velocity- or time-dependent, non-central, non-potential, constrained, colliding, external-force and many-body models) together with the status of the model data. The item adopts a modelling class; it asserts no law of nature, no measured value and no conservation law."

post-cm05-gravity.title: "Adopted two-label gravitational model: the inverse-square pair potential with coupling parameters, the empirical mass identification, and the measured value and uncertainty of the Newtonian constant"
post-cm05-gravity.physical_scope: "Adoption of the two-label gravitational model inside the page's central-force class: the inverse-square static pair potential with the Newtonian constant and positive gravitational coupling parameters; the empirical identification of the coupling parameters with the inertial masses, adopted as an assumption of the page's applications; the measured value of the Newtonian constant with its uncertainty and the mutual inconsistency of its measurements; and the non-relativistic weak-field two-point-label scope with its exclusions. The item adopts model data and empirical premises; it asserts no law of nature, no proof of the identification, and no numerical prediction by itself."

post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law.title: "Adopted ideal-reaction law for holonomic constraints: the d'Alembert condition, its scope and its limits"
post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law.physical_scope: "Adoption of the ideal-reaction law for the holonomic-constraint models of the force branch: along every constrained motion the reaction annihilates every virtual displacement at fixed time, equivalently it is a transpose multiple of the constraint Jacobian. The item records the modelled mechanisms and the exclusions (sliding friction along admissible directions, unilateral and contact-change mechanisms, rank loss, active drives, mechanical capability of the reaction) and separates the virtual-work condition from statements about actual work and energy. No measured value and no conservation claim is asserted."

post-cm11-heavy-top.title: "Adoption of the heavy symmetric top branch: axisymmetric rigid material, a fixed pivot material point, a uniform gravitational field and the balance of angular momentum about the pivot"
post-cm11-heavy-top.physical_scope: "Adoption of the heavy symmetric top branch of the rigid-material model: a reference mass distribution whose body inertia matrix is diag(A_c,A_c,C_c) about a declared symmetry axis, a material point held fixed at the origin of the inertial frame (the pivot, on the symmetry axis at distance d from the centre of mass, so that the centre of mass is constrained to the circle of radius d about the pivot), an ideal pivot mechanism contributing no torque about the pivot in the framework's sense of a frictionless hinge, a uniform gravitational field of magnitude g directed along $-e_3$, and the adopted balance of angular momentum about the pivot. The branch excludes friction and driving torques at the pivot, rolling and sliding contacts, non-axisymmetric bodies and non-uniform fields, and asserts no measured value and no claim that a concrete top or gyroscope realises it."

post-cm11-torque-balance.title: "Adoption of the external-torque branch of the rigid-material model: declared torque data and the balance of angular momentum about the centre of mass"
post-cm11-torque-balance.physical_scope: "Adoption of the external-torque branch of the rigid-material model branch of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: a declared continuous external-torque datum $\\tau:I_0\\to\\mathbb R^3$ (dimension $\\mu\\ell^{2}\\tau^{-2}$, newton metres), read as the total external torque about the centre of mass, and the adopted balance $L_c'=\\tau$ of the angular momentum about the centre of mass. The postulate asserts no force law producing $\\tau$, no balance for the centre-of-mass motion, no conservation law, no uniformity of rotation and no measured torque or observation; the countable-choice assumption is carried only for the finiteness of the defining integrals of the model's angular momentum. The branch excludes deformable bodies, impacts and variable mass; friction, contact and drive torques must be declared as part of $\\tau$ with their own models."

post-cm15-impulse.title: "Adopted impact and open-mass extensions of the force branch: the isolated reciprocal impulse model, the collinear restitution contact law and the open-body material accounting"
post-cm15-impulse.physical_scope: "Adoption of the page's impact and open-mass extensions of the framework's force branch: an isolated reciprocal impulse at one time (a finite momentum jump of opposite sign for the two labels, with the regular dynamics retained away from that time), a collinear restitution contact law with coefficient $0\\le e\\le1$ fixing only the relative velocity, and an open-body material accounting for matter entering and leaving a body at given rates with given inertial velocities. The item adopts model extensions and names their mathematical renderings; it derives nothing from the smooth-force postulates, asserts no law of nature, no measured value for $e$, the impulse or the mass rates, and excludes simultaneous contacts, friction, deformation modes and coefficients outside $[0,1]$."

post-cm17-contact-force-model.title: "Adopted force model of the continuum branch: continuous body forces and Cauchy contact tractions"
post-cm17-contact-force-model.physical_scope: "Adoption of the force description of the continuum branch: a continuous body-force field per unit mass on the swept region and a continuous traction field, force per unit area, depending on a contact surface only through its unit normal at the point (Cauchy's hypothesis). The postulate excludes couple stresses, nonlocal contact interactions, curvature-dependent contact forces, and electromagnetic, thermal or chemical forces; it asserts no balance law, no constitutive relation and no measured value."

post-cm17-fluid-constitutive.title: "Adopted fluid constitutive branches: incompressible Newtonian, barotropic inviscid, and the periodic-cell idealization"
post-cm17-fluid-constitutive.physical_scope: "Adoption of the fluid constitutive branches of the continuum framework: an incompressible Newtonian model with constant density, divergence-free velocity, pressure and positive dynamic viscosity; a barotropic inviscid model with a pressure law, conservative body force and enthalpy; and the periodic-cell idealization on the three-torus used by the local well-posedness theorem. The postulate excludes compressible viscosity with thermal coupling, non-Newtonian and turbulent-closure models, surface tension and multiphase flow, and asserts no measured viscosity, pressure law or boundary condition."

post-cm17-linear-elastic-constitutive.title: "Adopted isotropic linear elastic constitutive model with its small-strain regime and strain energy"
post-cm17-linear-elastic-constitutive.physical_scope: "Adoption of the small-strain isotropic linear elastic constitutive branch: displacement field, linear strain, stress matrix lambda (tr e) I + 2 mu_s e with positive-definite moduli, and the elastic strain-energy density with its positivity. The postulate states the small-strain kinematic idealization, the constancy of the reference density and the validity limits (small strains relative to a stress-free reference state, isothermal, no plasticity, viscosity, damage or coupling); it asserts no measured modulus, no boundary condition and no dynamical claim."

post-cm17-momentum-balance.title: "Adopted balance principles of the continuum model: force and couple-free torque balance on every admissible region"
post-cm17-momentum-balance.physical_scope: "Adoption of the balance principles of the continuum branch in force form: on every admissible bounded piecewise C-one region inside the current region, the surface traction resultant balances minus the volume integral of the body force minus the inertial term rho a, and the corresponding torque about any fixed origin balances likewise with no body or surface couples. The postulate excludes couple stresses, electromagnetic momentum exchange, mass sources and non-inertial frames; it asserts no constitutive law, no existence of a stress matrix and no measured value."

pthm-cm02-continuation.title: "Maximal Newtonian motions and the compact-continuation criterion: finite-time breakdown requires escape from every compact subset of the state domain"
pthm-cm02-continuation.physical_scope: "The continuation and breakdown criterion for the adopted Newtonian force model: the maximal motion of an initial datum is unique; at a finite right endpoint of its maximal interval its state graph leaves every compact subset of the open state domain, so a finite-time breakdown is caused by escape of the state (unbounded positions or velocities, or positions approaching the excluded configurations of the domain) or by the declared end of a finite time window; an autonomous force whose state is trapped in a compact subset of the state domain extends past the putative endpoint. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted force postulate and the cited mathematical continuation theorems; it asserts no global existence for particular force laws, no empirical statement and no claim that any physical system realizes the model."

pthm-cm02-ivp.title: "Local existence and uniqueness for the Newtonian initial-value problem, with the quantitative Picard-Lindelöf cylinder"
pthm-cm02-ivp.physical_scope: "The local existence, uniqueness and maximal-extension statement for the adopted Newtonian force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] on an open configuration domain: every initial datum with a configuration in the domain and an arbitrary coordinate velocity admits a unique motion through it, locally in time, and there is a unique maximal motion of which every motion with that datum is a restriction. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted force postulate and the cited mathematical ODE theorems; it gives no global existence, no bound on the interval, no empirical statement and no claim that any physical system realizes the model."

pthm-cm03-angular-momentum-balance.title: "Angular momentum balance about a fixed or moving reference point, the internal torque sum, and the centrality case"
pthm-cm03-angular-momentum-balance.physical_scope: "The angular momentum balance of a model that declares the external-plus-pair presentation with antisymmetric pair forces: the internal torque sum is independent of the reference point and the balance about a possibly moving reference point carries the correction minus odot cross P; when the evaluated pair forces are central the internal torque sum vanishes; about a fixed point with vanishing external torque the angular momentum is constant. The result is conditional on the declared pair structure and centrality where invoked; it asserts no necessity of centrality and no measured value."

pthm-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-kinetic-spl.title: "Total momentum equals total mass times centre-of-mass velocity, and the kinetic energy splits into centre-of-mass and relative parts (two-body reduced mass)"
pthm-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-kinetic-spl.physical_scope: "The algebraic identities of a curve family of a force model in one inertial frame: the total momentum is the total mass times the centre-of-mass velocity, the mass-weighted relative positions sum to zero together with their derivatives, and the total kinetic energy equals the centre-of-mass kinetic energy plus the mass-weighted relative kinetic energy, with the two-body reduced-mass form. The result is a conditional identity for the model's masses and curves and asserts no conservation law, no force structure and no measured value."

pthm-cm03-energy-balance.title: "Mechanical energy balance for a potential presentation: $E'=\\partial_tU$ plus the residual power, conservation for a static potential with no residual forces, and the integrated work form"
pthm-cm03-energy-balance.physical_scope: "The mechanical energy balance of a model presented through a potential with declared residual forces: the derivative of the mechanical energy equals the partial time derivative of the potential plus the power of the residual forces; a time-independent potential with no residual forces conserves the mechanical energy along every motion; and the integrated form expresses the work of the total force through the change of the potential and the residual work. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted potential presentation, with the normalization of the potential carried along; it asserts no measured value and no conservation outside the stated hypotheses."

pthm-cm03-frame-transformations.title: "Transformation of the state quantities under a change of inertial frame: centre of mass, total momentum, kinetic energy, angular momentum, torque, power, work and mechanical energy"
pthm-cm03-frame-transformations.physical_scope: "The transformation laws of the model's mechanical quantities under a change of inertial frame: the centre of mass and centre-of-mass velocity transform affinely, the total momentum gains M times the boost velocity, the kinetic energy gains a cross term and the boost kinetic energy, the angular momentum about corresponding points gains a boost term, and the torque, power and work transform according to the transferred force map of the force postulate; for a globally potential model whose potential is transferred by the scalar rule, the mechanical energy gains the same kinetic boost terms. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted frame, worldline and force laws; it asserts no invariance of these quantities and no measured value."

pthm-cm03-momentum-balance.title: "Total momentum balance and centre-of-mass equation for a model with antisymmetric pair forces"
pthm-cm03-momentum-balance.physical_scope: "The momentum balance of a model that declares the external-plus-pair force presentation with antisymmetric pair forces: along every motion the total momentum changes at the rate of the total external force, it is constant on an interval exactly when the total external force vanishes there, and the centre of mass obeys the single-particle equation with the total mass and the total external force. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted force and interaction posts; it asserts no conservation for models without the antisymmetry presentation and no measured value."

pthm-cm03-work-energy.title: "Power of the total force and the work-energy theorem: $K'=\\mathcal P$ and $K(t_1)-K(t_0)=W([t_0,t_1])$ along a motion"
pthm-cm03-work-energy.physical_scope: "The work-energy identity of the force branch: along every motion the time derivative of the kinetic energy equals the power of the total force, and the change of kinetic energy over a time interval equals the work of the total force. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted equation of motion and uses no potential, no pair structure and no conservation hypothesis; it asserts no frame-independent value and no measured quantity."

pthm-cm04-conservative-motion-and-energy.title: "Existence, uniqueness and conservation of energy for a one-dimensional conservative model: phase curves lie in energy level sets and the velocity is determined by the position"
pthm-cm04-conservative-motion-and-energy.physical_scope: "The basic dynamical content of a conservative one-dimensional model: every datum has exactly one maximal motion; the mechanical energy k x-dot^2/2 + U(x) (written m x-dot^2/2 + U(x)) is constant along every motion; a motion of initial energy E_0 keeps its position in the sublevel set {U <= E_0}, and where U is strictly below E_0 its velocity is one of the two square-root values determined by the position; every non-turning phase point of the motion lies on the energy level set of E_0; and the constant motions are exactly the rest motions at equilibria. The result is a conditional deduction from the declared potential presentation; it asserts no periodicity, no boundedness of the motion, no asymptotic behaviour and no measured value."

pthm-cm04-damped-decay-and-stability.title: "Strictly damped oscillator: explicit decay bounds, convergence to rest and asymptotic stability of the origin"
pthm-cm04-damped-decay-and-stability.physical_scope: "The strictly damped oscillator with m>0, k>0, c>0: every motion is bounded by explicit constants times the initial phase norm, tends to zero together with its velocity, and the origin of the phase plane is a globally asymptotically stable rest point in the sense of the framework's stability definition. The result is a conditional deduction from the declared model data; it asserts no value of the parameters, no measured decay rate and no behaviour of any real damper, and its constants are the explicit ones produced by the classification."

pthm-cm04-damped-motion.title: "Classification of the motions of the damped oscillator by the discriminant, and strict energy dissipation $E'=-c\\,x'^{2}$"
pthm-cm04-damped-motion.physical_scope: "The motion classification of the damped oscillator model with m>0, k>0, c>=0: the three solution families determined by the sign of the discriminant c^2-4mk (distinct real roots, double root, oscillatory roots), uniqueness and global existence for every datum, the identity E'=-c x-dot^2 for the mechanical energy k-dot-free part, the monotone decrease of the energy, and the characterisation of the constant-energy motions as the rest motion when c>0. The result is a conditional deduction from the declared model data; it asserts no value of the parameters, no measured decay and no behaviour of any real damper."

pthm-cm04-equilibrium-stability-at-a-str.title: "A strict local minimum of the potential is a Lyapunov stable equilibrium of the conservative one-dimensional model, and its linearisation is an oscillator-type model"
pthm-cm04-equilibrium-stability-at-a-str.physical_scope: "The equilibrium theory of a conservative one-dimensional model near a strict local minimum of its potential: the rest point is Lyapunov stable, with the Euclidean phase-plane norm, and its linearisation is the oscillator-type model with data (m,0,U''(x_*),0), which is the harmonic model with spring constant U''(x_*) when that number is positive. The statement is conditional on the declared potential and its strict local minimum; it asserts no asymptotic stability, no attraction and no instability in any case, and no measured value."

pthm-cm04-harmonic-motion.title: "The motions of the harmonic model are the sinusoids $A\\cos(\\omega(t-t_0))+B\\sin(\\omega(t-t_0))$: amplitude and phase, the least period, the conserved energy $kR^2/2$ and the elliptical phase curves"
pthm-cm04-harmonic-motion.physical_scope: "The complete motion analysis of the harmonic model with m>0 and k>0: every motion is a sinusoid about any chosen base time, with the initial data as coefficients; the amplitude and phase form; the least period 2 pi/omega and the frequency in cycles per second; the conserved mechanical energy k R^2/2; the phase curve is exactly the ellipse of the energy level set, with the two semiaxes; and the origin is the unique rest point and is Lyapunov stable. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted linear force law; it asserts no value of k or m, no application to a real spring, and no asymptotic stability."

pthm-cm04-resonance-and-boundedness.title: "The driven oscillator: the sinusoidal steady response, its amplitude and maximum, bounded motions for $c>0$ and at $c=0$ off resonance, and the unbounded resonant motions at $c=0$"
pthm-cm04-resonance-and-boundedness.physical_scope: "The response of the driven oscillator model with m>0, k>0, c>=0, drive amplitude f_0 and angular frequency Omega>0: the explicit steady sinusoidal response and its amplitude |f_0|/sqrt((k-m Omega^2)^2+c^2 Omega^2) whenever the denominator does not vanish; the reduction of every motion to the steady response plus a homogeneous motion; boundedness of every motion in the strictly damped case, with exponential convergence of the transient to the steady response; boundedness for c=0 away from Omega=sqrt(k/m); unbounded motions at c=0 and Omega=sqrt(k/m) with nonzero amplitude, so boundedness fails exactly in the off-singular-case sense; and the amplitude maximum of the steady response for c>0. The result is a conditional deduction from the declared drive and damping models; it asserts no measured resonance curve, no value of any parameter and no behaviour of an apparatus."

pthm-cm05-circular-orbit.title: "Circular relative orbits of the central model: the critical-point criterion $u'(r_0)=J^2/(\\mu r_0^3)$, uniform rotation of both labels about the centre of mass, and the linearised radial frequency"
pthm-cm05-circular-orbit.physical_scope: "Circular relative motion in the adopted central model: the critical-point condition of the effective potential, stated equivalently as the balance $\\mu r_0\\omega^2=u'(r_0)$ between the central force and the circular motion; the explicit uniform rotation of the relative coordinate and of both labels about the centre of mass; the necessity of the condition for a constant separation; and the frequency of the linearised radial equation at a minimum of the effective potential. The linearised clause is a statement about the quadratic approximation only; no nonlinear stability, no existence of circular orbits at arbitrary radii and no empirical claim is made."

pthm-cm05-conic.title: "The gravitational relative orbit is a conic focused at the force centre: $\\rho=p/(1+e\\cos(\\theta-\\theta_0))$, $E=(\\mu\\kappa^2/2J^2)(e^2-1)$, elliptic completeness and barycentric scaled ellipses"
pthm-cm05-conic.physical_scope: "The Keplerian orbit classification of the two-label gravitational model with non-zero angular momentum: the polar conic with its eccentricity and focus at the force centre, the eccentricity-energy relation and the elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic branches, the centrifugal barrier that keeps the motion away from the collision, and - in the elliptic case - the completeness, the closed periodic relative orbit with the ellipse geometry, and the scaled barycentric conics of both labels. The parabolic and hyperbolic clauses record only the orbit formula, the periapsis and the domain of the angle on the actual domain of the motion; no asymptotic extent, scattering or observational claim is made."

pthm-cm05-effective-potential.title: "Reduction of the central problem to the effective one-dimensional potential: $\\mu\\rho''=-(U^{\\mathrm{eff}}_J)'(\\rho)$, the energy identity, and the converse reconstruction of the planar trajectory from the radial data"
pthm-cm05-effective-potential.physical_scope: "The one-dimensional reduction of the non-radial central problem in the adopted model class: the radial coordinate obeys the effective-potential equation with the centrifugal barrier, its energy is the constant first integral of that one-dimensional problem, and conversely every positive radial solution together with the angular quadrature reconstructs a planar central-force trajectory with the prescribed angular momentum, hence a motion of the two-label model together with a uniform centre-of-mass motion. The result is a conditional deduction; it asserts no observation, no measured value, and no global existence for either side."

pthm-cm05-kepler-period.title: "Kepler's third law for the gravitational two-label model: the relative period is $T=2\\pi\\mu ab/J=2\\pi\\sqrt{\\mu/\\kappa}\\,a^{3/2}$, so $T^2=4\\pi^2a^3/(G_{\\mathrm N}M)$ under the mass identification, and both labels are periodic relative to the centre of mass"
pthm-cm05-kepler-period.physical_scope: "The period of the negative-energy gravitational relative orbit in the adopted two-label model: the relative motion is periodic, its period is $2\\pi\\mu ab/J=2\\pi\\sqrt{\\mu/\\kappa}\\,a^{3/2}$, the form $T^2=4\\pi^2a^3/(G_{\\mathrm N}M)$ holds when the gravitational couplings are identified with the inertial masses, each label is periodic about the centre of mass while its absolute motion advances by $VT$ per period, and the area swept per period is $\\pi ab$. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted model and its declared empirical identification; it reports no observation and no measured value."

pthm-cm05-plane-area.title: "Planarity of the reduced orbit and the area law: the areal-velocity vector is the constant $j/(2\\mu)$, the swept-area rate is $J/(2\\mu)$, and both labels sweep equal areas in equal times about the centre of mass"
pthm-cm05-plane-area.physical_scope: "The planar character of the reduced two-body orbit and the areal law, conditional on the adopted central-force model class: the attached angular-momentum vector is constant and orthogonal to the trajectory; for non-zero angular momentum the areal-velocity vector equals the constant $j/(2\\mu)$ and the swept-area function grows linearly; and each label sweeps a constant areal rate about the centre of mass with the mass-ratio factor $(m_2/m_1)^2$. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted model; it reports no observation, no measured value and no conservation beyond the conserved angular momentum of the central model."

pthm-cm05-relative-reduction.title: "Two-body reduction of a static central pair-potential model: the relative coordinate is a central-force trajectory for the reduced mass, the centre of mass moves uniformly, and the reconstruction is a bijection"
pthm-cm05-relative-reduction.physical_scope: "The conditional reduction of a two-label model whose force map is presented by a static central pair potential: along every motion the evaluated pair forces are central and antisymmetric, the total momentum and the centre-of-mass velocity are constant, the relative coordinate satisfies the one-body central-force equation with the reduced mass, and the motion is reconstructed from the centre-of-mass motion and the relative trajectory. The result is a deduction inside the adopted force and interaction branches; it uses no measured value, assumes no external forces, excludes collisions, and asserts no conservation law beyond the vanishing of the total external force that the presentation supplies."

pthm-cm06-inertial-forces.title: "The equation of motion in a moving chart: inertial terms, the inertial forces, and the exact criterion for a chart to be inertial"
pthm-cm06-inertial-forces.physical_scope: "The conditional description of the motions of a force-branch model in a rigidly moving and rotating spatial chart: the exact identity for the coordinate acceleration with the four inertial terms, the reading of those terms as mass-proportional inertial forces, and the characterization of exactly inertial charts as the charts whose inertial terms vanish, in which case the framework's force-covariance law is recovered. The inertial terms are properties of the chart's motion, not forces of the model's force map; the item asserts no equivalence between a moving chart and a gravitational field, and no measured value."

pthm-cm06-multiplier-balance.title: "Ideal holonomic constraints determine the reaction: multiplier form, explicit acceleration, unique constrained motions and the reaction-power identity"
pthm-cm06-multiplier-balance.physical_scope: "The conditional dynamics of a holonomic-constraint model with the adopted ideal-reaction law: the reaction is the transpose multiple of the constraint Jacobian with a unique continuous multiplier, the multiplier and the constrained acceleration are the explicit functions Lambda and a of the datum, the constrained motions with permitted velocity are exactly the solutions of the resulting first-order system with consistent data, the constraint and its differentiated form are preserved, and the reaction power equals minus the multiplier paired with the time derivative of the constraint. Empirical qualifications of the idealization and the exclusions of the postulate are carried; no measured value and no energy-conservation claim is asserted."

pthm-cm06-rheonomic-power.title: "Reaction work and mechanical-energy balance for ideal holonomic constraints: vanishing power for scleronomic constraints and the rheonomic work term"
pthm-cm06-rheonomic-power.physical_scope: "The work and energy statements of an ideal holonomic-constraint model with an ambient force map presented through a potential with residual forces: the reaction power equals minus the multiplier paired with the time derivative of the constraint, so scleronomic ideal constraints perform no work, while rheonomic ideal constraints can change the mechanical energy through a term that is not a residual force of the model; the mechanical-energy balance carries that term, conservation holds only for a scleronomic constraint with a static potential and no residual forces, and the integrated work form is stated. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted model and idealization, with the empirical qualifications of the ideal-reaction postulate carried; no measured value is asserted."

pthm-cm07-boundary-terms-and-gauge.title: "Total-derivative Lagrangians, the potential representative and scaling: invariant stationary curves with endpoint terms"
pthm-cm07-boundary-terms-and-gauge.physical_scope: "Gauge properties of the mechanical action of a declared potential presentation: adding to the Lagrangian the total time derivative of a C^2 function changes the action by endpoint values only and leaves the Euler-Lagrange expression, the stationary curves and the model's stationary-action equation unchanged; changing the potential representative by a function of time alone is an instance and shifts the action by a constant-free endpoint term; multiplying the Lagrangian by a nonzero constant leaves the stationary curves unchanged. The statements are conditional on the adopted force branch and presentation and assert no minimisation and no empirical content."

pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-e.title: "Time-dependent coordinate maps transform the model's equation into the Euler-Lagrange equation of the substituted Lagrangian"
pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-e.physical_scope: "Covariance of the model's equation of motion under a time-dependent coordinate map of the configuration domain: along a curve described by a C^3 map X with everywhere invertible configuration Jacobian, the Euler-Lagrange expression of the substituted Lagrangian is the transpose-Jacobian multiple of the inertial-chart expression, so the model's potential-part equation holds along the Cartesian description if and only if the substituted Euler-Lagrange equation holds along the coordinate description; when the chart condition holds, this is equivalent to stationarity of the substituted action. The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the potential presentation and the smooth invertibility of the coordinate map; it asserts nothing about constraints with fewer coordinates, which are treated separately, and no empirical claim."

pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations.title: "The Euler-Lagrange equation of the mechanical Lagrangian is the model's equation of motion, and the stationary-action criterion"
pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations.physical_scope: "The Euler-Lagrange equation of the mechanical Lagrangian of a declared potential presentation: for a C^2 curve of the model on a fixed interval, stationarity of the action, the vanishing of the Euler-Lagrange expression and the pointwise equation mass-operator acceleration equals minus the potential gradient are equivalent. The equivalence identifies the variational critical-point condition with the model's equation of motion on the interval; it is conditional on the adopted force branch and the declared presentation, and it asserts no solution existence, no minimisation and no empirical content."

pthm-cm07-first-variation-and-euler-lagr.title: "The first variation of the mechanical action and the Euler-Lagrange expression in model terms"
pthm-cm07-first-variation-and-euler-lagr.physical_scope: "The first variation of the action of a force model with a declared potential presentation, computed in the inertial chart: for every C^2 admissible curve and fixed-endpoint variation the variation exists and equals the integral of minus the potential gradient paired with the variation plus the mass-operator pairing of velocity with the variation's derivative, and the Euler-Lagrange expression of the mechanical Lagrangian is minus the sum of the mass-operator acceleration and the potential gradient. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared potential presentation and the cited mathematical first-variation formula; it asserts no equation of motion, which is the subject of the following items."

pthm-cm07-lagrangian-reduction-of-ideal-.title: "Ideal scleronomic holonomic constraints: the substituted Lagrange equations are equivalent to the constrained model equation"
pthm-cm07-lagrangian-reduction-of-ideal-.physical_scope: "The elimination of ideal scleronomic holonomic constraints by parametrization: for a global C^3 parametrization of the constrained configurations of a scleronomic regular holonomic datum, a C^2 coordinate curve describes an ideal constrained motion of the force model exactly when it solves the declared Lagrange equations of the substituted Lagrangian with the residual generalized force; the reaction is then uniquely determined, annihilates the virtual displacements and admits the unique continuous multiplier. The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the potential presentation, the constraint datum with its rank hypothesis and the ideal-reaction law; it asserts no solution existence, no uniqueness of the coordinate curve for given data and no empirical claim."

pthm-cm07-newton-equivalence.title: "Stationary curves of the mechanical action are exactly the restrictions of the model's motions (global potential branch)"
pthm-cm07-newton-equivalence.physical_scope: "The stationary-action principle for the global potential branch of the force model: every motion of the model restricts to a stationary curve of the mechanical action on each closed subinterval, and conversely every C^2 stationary curve on a closed interval is the restriction of the unique maximal motion of the model through its initial datum, so that the stationary curves are exactly the restrictions of motions. The equivalence is conditional on the adopted force branch, on the declared potential presentation with no residual forces, and on the cited existence, uniqueness and continuation theorems; it asserts no global existence, no minimisation property and no empirical statement."

pthm-cm08-boost-boundary.title: "The Galilean boost charge of the model: exact condition, uniform centre-of-mass motion, the induced motions and the boundary of the conservation law"
pthm-cm08-boost-boundary.physical_scope: "The Galilean boost charge of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: the time-dependent symmetry datum (tau, xi, B) = (0, t a, a . M x) satisfies the model's Noether identity exactly when the potential is invariant under the simultaneous translation of all labels by the vector a; in the global potential branch the boost charge a . (t P - M X) is then constant, the component a of the centre of mass moves uniformly, and the boosted curves t -> x(t) + s t a of motions are again motions; for an arbitrary presentation the exact rate of the charge is the time times the component a of the total force, and a nonzero translation derivative of the potential at a nonzero time produces a motion along which the charge is not constant. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared potential and the absence of residual forces in the conservation clauses; it asserts no boost invariance of any particular force law and carries no empirical content."

pthm-cm08-general-noether.title: "The general Noether theorem of the model: point transformations with time reparametrisation, the charge $p\\cdot\\xi-E\\tau-B$, its residual-force rate and its potential gauge"
pthm-cm08-general-noether.physical_scope: "The general point Noether theorem of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: for a symmetry datum with time reparametrisation, the charge M x' . xi - (K+U) tau - B is constant along every motion of the global potential branch; the charge has derivative equal to the residual force paired with xi - x' tau for an arbitrary presentation; the tau=0 and xi=0, tau=1 specialisations reduce to the strict point-symmetry charge and to minus the mechanical energy; and replacing the potential representative U by U+c(t) with the boundary function B-c tau preserves the identity and leaves the charge unchanged. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the symmetry identity; it asserts no symmetry of any particular force law, no converse from conservation to symmetry, and carries no empirical content."

pthm-cm08-moving-chart-energy-function.title: "The energy function of a moving chart: exact difference from the inertial mechanical energy and conservation along the chart solutions"
pthm-cm08-moving-chart-energy-function.physical_scope: "The energy bookkeeping of a time-dependent coordinate description of the force model: for a C^3 coordinate map X with everywhere invertible configuration Jacobian and the substituted Lagrangian of the covariance theorem, the chart energy function equals the inertial mechanical energy plus or minus the pairing of the chart's explicit time dependence with the mass-operator velocity, so the two agree exactly when that pairing vanishes; the chart energy function is conserved along chart Euler-Lagrange solutions whenever the substituted Lagrangian has no explicit time dependence along the trajectory; and in the global potential branch the chart description of every motion solves that chart equation. The statement concerns the model's coordinate description, is conditional on the adopted force branch and the declared presentation, and asserts no measurement and no identification of the chart energy with the inertial mechanical energy."

pthm-cm08-point-noether.title: "The point Noether theorem of the model: conservation of the charge of a strict symmetry, and the residual-force rate"
pthm-cm08-point-noether.physical_scope: "The point Noether theorem of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: for a strict symmetry datum of the mechanical Lagrangian that is independent of time, the charge M x' . xi - B is constant along every motion of the global potential branch; for an arbitrary presentation the charge of a strict datum has derivative equal to the residual force paired with the generator, so conservation holds exactly when that pairing vanishes along the motion. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared presentation, the symmetry identity and, in the conservation clause, on the absence of residual forces; it asserts no symmetry of any particular force law and carries no empirical content."

pthm-cm08-rotation.title: "Rotation symmetry of the model's Lagrangian and conservation of angular momentum about the origin"
pthm-cm08-rotation.physical_scope: "Rotation symmetry of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: the equivalence between the differential invariance condition of the potential along the rotation family with axis a and finite invariance on admissible rotation arcs, with the exact component compatibility criterion for all admissible endpoints, the resulting strict symmetry datum, conservation of the component a . J of the total angular momentum about the inertial origin along every motion of the global potential branch, its sharpness under a nonzero rotational derivative of U, and the vector form when the potential is invariant under all rotations about the origin. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared potential and the absence of residual forces in the conservation clauses; it asserts no rotation symmetry of any particular force law and carries no empirical content."

pthm-cm08-time-energy.title: "Time translation and the mechanical energy of the model: conservation in the autonomous global potential branch and the sharp failure for a time-dependent potential"
pthm-cm08-time-energy.physical_scope: "Time translation as a symmetry datum of the force model with a declared potential presentation: the datum (tau,xi,B)=(1,0,0) satisfies the model's Noether identity exactly when the potential has no explicit time dependence; in the global potential branch with an autonomous potential the mechanical energy K+U is constant along every motion; and if the potential depends explicitly on time at a state, then the maximal motion through that state has nonvanishing energy derivative there, so the energy is not conserved. The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and the declared presentation; the sharpness clause uses the maximal-motion existence theorem, and no empirical content is asserted."

pthm-cm08-translation.title: "Translation symmetry of the model's Lagrangian and conservation of total momentum: exact hypothesis, conservation and its sharpness"
pthm-cm08-translation.physical_scope: "Translation symmetry of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: the exact equivalence between the differential invariance condition sum_i a . grad_i U = 0 and finite invariance on admissible translation segments, with the exact component compatibility criterion for all admissible endpoints, the resulting strict symmetry datum and conservation of the component a . P of the total momentum along every motion of the global potential branch, the sharpness statement that a nonzero directional derivative at a state produces a motion whose momentum component is not constant, and the vector form for a fully translation-invariant potential. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared potential and the absence of residual forces in the conservation clauses; it asserts no translation symmetry of any particular force law and carries no empirical content."

pthm-cm09-averaging-for-weak-damping.title: "Averaging for a weakly damped oscillator: the rotating-frame amplitude, the averaged exponential energy decay and the order-$\\varepsilon$ bound on the $O(1/\\varepsilon)$ time scale"
pthm-cm09-averaging-for-weak-damping.physical_scope: "The strictly damped one-dimensional oscillator model m x'' + epsilon gamma x' + k x = 0 with m>0, k>0, small parameter epsilon>0 and fixed gamma>0: the exact rotating-frame amplitude zeta(t) = (omega_0 x + i x') exp(i omega_0 t)/sqrt(2 omega_0) and its slow equation zeta' = epsilon F(t,zeta) with F smooth and periodic in time, the averaged equation zeta' = -(epsilon gamma/(2m)) zeta with the exponential averaged solution, the order-epsilon averaging estimate on the O(1/epsilon) time scale under the stated smallness, trapping and constant hypotheses, and the resulting exponential energy-decay estimate |E(t) - E_0 exp(-epsilon gamma t/m)| <= m omega_0 epsilon K (2|zeta_0|+epsilon K). The result is a conditional finite-time statement about the declared damped model; the averaged system is a different model compared with the exact one, no exact energy decay law is asserted, no measured decay rate or quality factor is reported and no empirical claim is made."

pthm-cm09-forced-modal-response.title: "The forced coupled quadratic model: decoupled modal responses, sinusoidal drive, resonance at the modal frequencies and boundedness away from resonance"
pthm-cm09-forced-modal-response.physical_scope: "The forced coupled quadratic model M q'' + K q = J(t) with symmetric positive definite mass metric, symmetric non-negative stiffness and a prescribed continuous generalized force: decoupling into independent scalar forced modal equations, the unique motion for every datum given by the modal convolution formulas, and the sinusoidal case J(t)=J_0 cos(Omega t) with the modal steady responses of amplitude |psi_0i|/|lambda_i-Omega^2|, the resonant unbounded motions at Omega^2=lambda_i with nonvanishing modal force component, the zero-mode cases (bounded for Omega>0 and quadratic growth for Omega=0), the reduction of every motion to a particular response plus a free motion, unboundedness of every motion in the resonant cases, and boundedness of every motion for positive definite stiffness away from resonance. The result is a conditional statement about the declared model with a prescribed external generalized force in the modelling status of a drive; it asserts no back-reaction of the source, no measured response, no damping and no empirical claim."

pthm-cm09-free-modes-and-degeneracy.title: "The free coupled quadratic model: global existence, the complete modal classification, mode energies, intrinsic degenerate mode subspaces, boundedness and the unstable direction"
pthm-cm09-free-modes-and-degeneracy.physical_scope: "The free coupled quadratic model M q'' + K q = 0 of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with symmetric positive definite mass metric M and symmetric stiffness K: existence and uniqueness of motions for every datum on the whole real line, the complete classification of motions into oscillatory, affine and exponential modal families with mode frequencies sqrt(lambda_i), the conservation of the mechanical energy with the modal energy decomposition, the intrinsic (basis-free) description of degenerate pure-lambda families in the subspace ker(K - lambda M), boundedness of every motion when K is positive definite, unbounded growth of the affine zero-mode motions and of the exponential directions, and the Lyapunov instability of the rest point of the free model when K has a negative modal stiffness. The result is a conditional statement about the declared model class; it contains no claim that any physical system is described by it, no measured stiffness, mass or frequency, and no empirical qualification beyond the exact idealization of the model."

pthm-cm09-linearization-at-a-strict-mini.title: "Small oscillations at a strict minimum: the linearized model, its normal modes and the Lyapunov stability of the nonlinear equilibrium"
pthm-cm09-linearization-at-a-strict-mini.physical_scope: "A mechanical system in a chart at a strict local minimum of its potential: the assigned small-oscillation quadratic model with mass metric M(q_0) and stiffness the Hessian D^2 U(q_0) (symmetric and non-negative), the identification of that model with the derivative linearization of the mechanical field, the complete normal-mode classification of the linearized motions with frequencies sqrt(lambda_i) and no exponential directions, and the Lyapunov stability of the nonlinear equilibrium by exact energy conservation. The stability conclusion is a statement about the declared chart model; it asserts no asymptotic attraction, no measured frequency, no particular physical system and no empirical claim, and the accuracy of the linear model as an approximation of the nonlinear motion is a separate finite-time statement on this page."

pthm-cm09-linearization-error-bound.title: "Finite-time error control for the small-oscillation approximation: the quadratic remainder of the mechanical field and the variation-of-constants bound"
pthm-cm09-linearization-error-bound.physical_scope: "Finite-time error control for the small-oscillation model of a mechanical system in a chart at a mechanical equilibrium: for a C^3 kinetic metric field and a C^3 potential with vanishing gradient at q_0, the mechanical field is C^2 near the equilibrium, its Taylor remainder at the linearization is quadratic with constants obtained from compactness, and the finite-time variation-of-constants estimate bounds the difference between the nonlinear motion and the linearized (normal-mode) motion by C delta^2 t exp((||A||+2L)t) on every horizon T with delta exp(LT)<r_0. The statement is a conditional finite-time estimate for the declared chart model under explicit regularity and smallness hypotheses; it asserts no all-time validity of the linear approximation, no stability conclusion, no large-data statement and no empirical claim, and the constants depend on the model data only through its behaviour on the stated ball."

pthm-cm11-euler-equations.title: "Euler's equations with torque for the rigid-material model, the rotational power identity, the torque-free reduction and frame covariance"
pthm-cm11-euler-equations.physical_scope: "Conditional deductions inside the external-torque branch of [[post-cm11-torque-balance]] for the rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: the body-frame Euler equations with the declared torque datum, their principal-axis components, the power identity $\\frac{d}{dt}\\tfrac12\\omega^{\\mathsf T}I\\omega=\\omega\\cdot R^{\\mathsf T}\\tau$ (and constancy of the rotational kinetic energy in the torque-free case), the torque-free reduction $l'=l\\times(I^{-1}l)$ under nondegeneracy, and the preservation of the balance under changes of inertial frame with the declared transformation of the torque datum. No force law producing $\\tau$, no conservation of $L_c$ (which is proved on the same page), no measurement and no empirical value is asserted."

pthm-cm11-linearized-spin.title: "Linearization of the torque-free spin of the rigid-material model at a principal-axis spin: the oscillatory/exponential dichotomy and linear stability"
pthm-cm11-linearized-spin.physical_scope: "The first-order linearization of the torque-free body-angular-velocity dynamics of a nondegenerate rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]] at a principal-axis spin $\\Omega e_j$, for pairwise distinct principal moments: the total derivative of the spin field, the explicit transverse equations, the sign criterion $\\lambda_j<0$ for an extreme axis and $\\lambda_j>0$ for the intermediate axis, the bounded oscillatory solutions in the extreme case and the exponentially growing solutions in the intermediate case, and the corresponding linear-stability verdicts in the sense of [[def-cm-orbital-and-linear-stability]]. The statement concerns the linearized system only; no nonlinear Lyapunov conclusion is drawn here, and no measurement, damping, friction or empirical value is asserted."

pthm-cm11-nonlinear-spin-stability.title: "Nonlinear stability of the torque-free spin of the rigid-material model about an extreme principal axis, and instability about the intermediate axis, with an explicit escape time and the orientation caveat"
pthm-cm11-nonlinear-spin-stability.physical_scope: "Lyapunov stability and instability of the torque-free spin of a nondegenerate rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]] with pairwise distinct principal moments, stated for the model's motions with time window containing $[0,\\infty)$: spins about the largest and smallest principal axes are Lyapunov stable in the body angular momentum, with an explicit conserved deviation bound, and spins about the intermediate axis are unstable with an explicit escape time; the escaping perturbation is realised by an actual torque-free motion. The stability is a statement about the body-frame angular momentum and angular velocity only: two motions with the same constant body angular velocity can have orientations differing by a fixed nontrivial rotation at every time, so no orientation stability is asserted. No measurement, damping, dissipation or empirical value is asserted; the countable-choice assumption is carried for the quaternion constructions."

pthm-cm11-principal-rotations.title: "Principal-axis uniform rotations of the torque-free rigid-material model: existence, the fixed spatial axis, the invariants, and the converse classification"
pthm-cm11-principal-rotations.physical_scope: "Conditional statements about the torque-free branch of a nondegenerate rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: for every principal axis $e_j$ and every real rate $\\Omega$ there is a motion whose orientation path is a uniform rotation with constant body angular velocity $\\Omega e_j$; for $\\Omega\\neq0$ the material axis $R(t)e_j$ is fixed in the inertial frame and the motion is a rotation about a fixed spatial direction; the invariants take the values $C=\\Omega^{2}I_j^{2}$, $E=\\tfrac12\\Omega^{2}I_j$; and conversely, a torque-free motion with constant body angular velocity must spin about a principal axis. The statements carry the countable-choice assumption used only to select the initial unit quaternion, assert no measurement, no empirical law and no claim that any apparatus has been observed."

pthm-cm11-top-reduction.title: "Reduction of the heavy symmetric top branch: pivotal angular momentum, Euler-angle equations, the two conserved momenta and the one-dimensional $\\theta$ equation"
pthm-cm11-top-reduction.physical_scope: "Conditional deductions inside the heavy symmetric top branch of [[post-cm11-heavy-top]] for the rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: the angular momentum about the pivot equals $R\\tilde I\\omega$ with $\\tilde I$ the inertia about the pivot; the pivot balance gives the body-frame equations; and on any interval on which the orientation is described by the Euler-angle chart with $\\theta\\in(0,\\pi)$ the motion satisfies the heavy-top system with parameters equal to the pivot transverse moment $A=A_c+md^{2}$, the axial moment $C=C_c$, the total mass $m$, the pivot distance $d$ and the field strength $g$, so the conserved momenta, the reduced energy and the one-dimensional $\\theta$ equation hold. The statement carries the countable-choice assumption used only for the finiteness of the defining integrals, assumes the chart description as an explicit hypothesis, asserts nothing at the chart's poles, excludes friction and driving torques at the pivot, and asserts no measured value."

pthm-cm11-torque-free-invariants.title: "Torque-free motion of the rigid-material model: conservation of the angular momentum about the centre of mass, the energy-momentum invariants, the principal-axis equations and global existence of the spin dynamics"
pthm-cm11-torque-free-invariants.physical_scope: "Conditional statements about a torque-free motion of a nondegenerate rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: the angular momentum about the centre of mass is constant in the inertial frame; the scalars $C=\\lVert l\\rVert_2^{2}=\\lVert L_c\\rVert_2^{2}$ and $E=\\tfrac12\\omega^{\\mathsf T}I\\omega=\\tfrac12 l\\cdot I^{-1}l$ are constants of the motion and $E$ is the rotational kinetic energy; in a principal basis the spin components obey the displayed torque-free equations; and the torque-free spin field is globally solvable in time, so the body angular momentum and the body angular velocity of a torque-free motion are bounded by initial data. The statements are conditional on the adopted zero-torque balance and nondegeneracy, carry the countable-choice assumption used only for the finiteness of the defining integrals, and assert no measurement, no orientation statement and no claim about nature."

pthm-cm12-energy-time.title: "The mechanical Hamiltonian is the model's energy in the inertial chart, its balance is the energy balance, and the substituted-chart Hamiltonian is the energy of time-independent coordinates"
pthm-cm12-energy-time.physical_scope: "The relation between the Hamiltonian of a declared potential presentation of the force branch and the model's mechanical energy: in the inertial Cartesian chart the branch Hamiltonian equals K + U along every curve, its time derivative along a motion is the explicit time dependence of the potential plus the power of the residual forces, and it is constant for a static potential with no residual forces; in a time-independent generalized-coordinate chart the substituted Hamiltonian is the same mechanical energy of the induced configuration curve. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured value and no conservation outside the stated hypotheses."

pthm-cm12-hamilton-equivalence.title: "Hamilton's equations of the mechanical presentation are equivalent to the model's equation of motion, with residual forces as momentum sources and the coordinate form on every chart"
pthm-cm12-hamilton-equivalence.physical_scope: "The equivalence between the Hamiltonian evolution of a declared potential presentation of the force branch and the model's equations of motion: on the potential branch the motions, the solutions of Hamilton's equations for the explicit branch Hamiltonian and the stationary curves of the action coincide; with residual forces the model's equation is equivalent to Hamilton's equations with the residual force as a momentum source; in a declared generalized-coordinate chart the declared Lagrange equations are equivalent to the Hamilton system, and for a scleronomic regular holonomic-constraint parametrization to the ideal constrained motion. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the presentation and the cited mathematics; it makes no existence, uniqueness or empirical claim."

pthm-cm12-local-legendre.title: "The velocity Hessian of the mechanical Lagrangian and the local invertibility of its Legendre map in every chart of the model"
pthm-cm12-local-legendre.physical_scope: "The Legendre map of a declared potential presentation of the force branch: the velocity Hessian of the mechanical Lagrangian in an inertial Cartesian chart and in a declared generalized-coordinate chart, its positivity, the resulting velocity-regularity at every state, and the existence of a local C^1 inverse branch at every state of those charts. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no global inverse branch on a momentum fibre, no equation of motion, no conservation law and no measured value."

pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity.title: "Every potential presentation is hyperregular in its charts, with inverse branch $v = \\mathsf M^{-1}p$ (or $G(q)^{-1}p$) and the explicit kinetic-plus-potential Hamiltonian"
pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity.physical_scope: "Globality of the Legendre transformation of a declared potential presentation of the force branch: the velocity-to-momentum maps of the Cartesian chart and of a declared generalized-coordinate chart are C^2 bijections of each velocity fibre onto the full momentum fibre, with the explicit C^2 inverse branches v = M^{-1}p and v = G(q)^{-1}p, and the Hamiltonians of those branches have the explicit kinetic-plus-potential forms. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law and no measured value."

pthm-cm13-bracket-identities.title: "The bracket of a potential presentation is bilinear, skew, a derivation in each slot, satisfies the Jacobi identity, and reproduces the fundamental brackets and the Hamiltonian field"
pthm-cm13-bracket-identities.physical_scope: "The algebraic identities of the Poisson bracket of a declared potential presentation: bilinearity, skew-symmetry, the Leibniz rule in each slot, the Jacobi identity for $C^{3}$ phase functions, the identity $\\{f,g\\}=X_g(f)$ relating the bracket to the presentation's Hamiltonian fields, and the fundamental brackets of the model's canonical coordinates. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law and no measured value."

pthm-cm13-dynamics-transport-under-canon.title: "Canonical maps of a potential presentation conjugate the Hamiltonian fields and transport the model's Hamiltonian systems and brackets"
pthm-cm13-dynamics-transport-under-canon.physical_scope: "Transformation theory for the declared potential presentation: a $C^{2}$ canonical map conjugates the Hamiltonian field of a phase function to the field of the composed function, preserves the model's Poisson bracket under composition, and carries solutions of one Hamiltonian system to solutions of the other, also for time-dependent Hamiltonians. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical content and no global existence of canonical maps."
